ogTitle: 10 Most Popular Restaurants in Trang 2026 — Eat Like a Local
ogDesc: Crispy roast pork, morning dim sum, ancient coffee, Kantang seafood, and the original Trang cake — the restaurants locals in Trang really eat at, all in one list.
eyebrow: Eat Like a Trang Local · Updated 2026
intro: Trang is a city that wakes up to eat together. Crispy roast pork, steaming baskets of dim sum, and a strong cup of kophi ancient coffee are the morning ritual that binds the whole province. Come evening, there are jok kuay and seaside seafood to follow. We've gathered 10 restaurants locals genuinely eat at — from the old-town legends of Thap Thieng to the original Trang cake in Lamphura.

blocks.html:
The magic of Trang is its rhythm of eating — unlike anywhere else. People here meet for breakfast before daylight. In the old Thap Thieng quarter around Huay Yot and Phloen Phithak roads, roast-pork shops and dim-sum restaurants switch their lights on from five in the morning. The smell of crispy-skin roast pork drifts out alongside steam rising from bamboo dim-sum baskets. On the table, a strong dark cup of kophi is waiting to wake you up. This is Hainanese Chinese culture that has put down roots here across generations. Move beyond the city toward Kantang and you find fresh seafood right by the pier. Out in Lamphura and Huay Yot, there is Trang cake — soft, egg-rich, with a hole in the middle, uniced — to take home. A full day of eating in Trang is like touring the whole city through its plates.

Several restaurants on this list are genuine local institutions. Trang Moo Yang on Huay Yot Road has been open since 1994, serving its crispy roast pork with dim sum — a breakfast that generations of Trang people grew up with. Ruean Thai Dim Sum on Phloen Phithak is consistently rated one of the province's top dim sum spots. Moo Yang Ko Phao in the municipal fresh market sells out before 9 a.m. on most days. Ko Choi is a Thai-Chinese restaurant over fifty years old, famous for red-braised pork leg and bitter gourd curry. Phong Ocha fills a single restaurant with over two hundred types of dim sum. And Cake Khuk Ming in Lamphura is the true originator of Trang cake — a dense egg cake with a hole in the centre, no cream, no icing. Every restaurant here is open and waiting for you to try it yourself.

blocks.name: Trang Moo Yang
blocks.area: Huay Yot Road, Thap Thieng Sub-district, Mueang Trang District, Trang Province
blocks.signature: Trang crispy-skin roast pork — sweet-leading with a gentle salty finish — served with dim sum and ancient coffee
blocks.descHtml:
If you're in Trang and want to pack the province's most iconic bites into one meal, Trang Moo Yang on Huay Yot Road is where locals take out-of-town friends most often. This long-established restaurant has been open for decades — a shophouse in the heart of Thap Thieng old quarter, trading from early morning until noon. It's the ideal way to start a day the Southern Thai way: sit down with ancient coffee, stack the table with dim sum, then finish with the house highlight — crispy-skin roast pork.

The dish that everyone orders is Trang roast pork: chunky cuts, crispy skin, tender flesh, flavoured with a sweetness-first seasoning followed by a gentle salty note and fragrant Chinese spices — something hard to find elsewhere. Reviews consistently say the pork pieces are generous and the house dipping sauce is distinctive — sweet-sour with a hint of chilli, different from the standard. The fried spring rolls are also widely praised as unusually good. For dim sum there are shrimp shumai, soft-boiled eggs, and more, served alongside a hot cup of kophi — the combination lands perfectly for a Southern Thai breakfast.

The atmosphere is entirely old-school — a charcoal roasting station visible from the front, tables filling up fast on weekend mornings. Prices are approachable; most regulars describe it as budget-friendly, typically a few hundred baht per person. Ordering the roast pork by the kilogram to share around the table is good value.

Worth knowing: the restaurant sells only in the morning until noon. Popular items like the roast pork sell out early. If you have a specific order in mind, come early for freshness and avoid trying to park on Huay Yot Road on weekends — space is limited. This is the ideal first meal of a Trang trip: roast pork, dim sum, and ancient coffee in one place.
blocks.bestFor: The first breakfast of your Trang trip
blocks.spice: Mild (dipping sauce is sweet-sour with a gentle hint of chilli)

blocks.name: Ruean Thai Dim Sum
blocks.area: Phloen Phithak Road, Thap Thieng Sub-district, Mueang Trang District, Trang Province
blocks.signature: Hot steamed dim sum in multiple baskets, Hoy Cho Crab, Trang Roast Pork
blocks.descHtml:
If you want to start a new morning in Trang the right way, many people nominate Ruean Thai Dim Sum as the first stop. This long-standing dim sum restaurant, a multi-generation family business managed by the Chuengjit family (Theerasak and Chareeni), is known for its bamboo baskets of hot steamed dim sum laid out for self-selection — from shumai and har gao to char siu buns, prawn-filled, crab-filled, and inventive handmade varieties. It's ideal for a relaxed family or group breakfast, picking basket after basket at your own pace.

The dish everyone orders is Trang roast pork — crispy skin, a sweet-forward flavour that is authentically Trang. Then there's the crab hoy cho — firm, packed with crab — freshly fried pa thong ko with custard for dipping, and a smooth, rounded congee or bak kut teh. Reviews broadly praise the dim sum arriving hot with bouncy texture and quality ingredients. The roast pork suits those who like sweet-leading flavours; a few reviews note that on some days the pork can be slightly chewy, but overall this is a restaurant that locals and visitors return to repeatedly.

Prices are friendly — dim sum baskets start around 25 THB; a plate of roast pork runs low hundreds. An average of 100–250 THB per person is enough to eat well. The restaurant is large, with wide round tables that accommodate tour groups and big families. Located on Phloen Phithak Road opposite the Ford showroom, in the city centre. Easy to find, parking available.

Worth knowing: this is strictly a breakfast restaurant, open roughly 06:00 until noon. By mid-morning the baskets thin out — arrive before 10:30 for the best selection. The pick-your-own-basket system can be a little confusing at first, but it quickly becomes fun.
mustOrder: Hot Steamed Dim Sum in Multiple Baskets
Pa Thong Ko with Custard Dip
blocks.bestFor: Morning dim sum — family or group breakfast

blocks.name: Moo Yang Ko Phao
blocks.area: Nakhon Trang Municipal Fresh Market, Mueang Trang District, Trang Province
blocks.signature: Thin crispy-skin roast pork, fragrant with spices — sold by the kilogram, take home
blocks.priceRange: Sold by the kilogram, hundreds of THB per kg (half-kg orders accepted)
blocks.descHtml:
If you're in Trang and want the real thing — authentic Trang-style roast pork — the name that locals say first is Moo Yang Ko Phao, a small stall at the back of the Nakhon Trang municipal fresh market. This stall has been there for decades, with a three-generation recipe passed down intact. It's for anyone who wants to eat the province's signature, take it home as a gift, or snap off a piece with morning coffee the Trang way.

The order is sliced roast pork, sold by weight. The skin is thin and crispy, the marinade penetrates fully so the colour is deep and even, fragrant with Chinese aromatics, a trace of five-spice and a honey-like sweetness. Reviews consistently say the marinade reaches through the meat, so it tastes good completely on its own without dipping sauce. Some love the puffed, crispy skin; a few reviews note that spice intensity can vary piece to piece, which is normal for a handmade, char-roasted product.

The setting is a traditional fresh-market stall — look for the prominent red signage. Prices are per kilogram, running in the hundreds of baht per kg (fluctuates with season). Half-kilogram orders are accepted. Vacuum packaging is available for taking home. Located in the Nakhon Trang Municipal Market, city centre — walkable from most older hotels.

Popular because the stall opens before dawn — roasting starts in the middle of the night, selling from around 5:00–6:30 a.m. every day. Queues form before opening and it's typically sold out before 8–9 a.m. For a reliable order, call ahead (086 277 8327), place a reservation, and collect early — that's the most foolproof approach.
mustOrder: Sliced Crispy-skin Roast Pork (by the kilogram)
Vacuum-packed to take home as a souvenir
blocks.bestFor: Very early breakfast and buying the province's souvenir to take home
blocks.hours: Opens very early ~05:00–06:30 daily, sold out before 08:00–09:00
blocks.spice: Not spicy (fragrant spice aroma, sweet-salty Trang roast-pork style)

blocks.name: Ko Choi
blocks.signature: Red-braised Pork Leg, Bitter Gourd Curry with Sea Bass and Young Coconut Shoot, Shrimp Stir-fried with Shrimp Paste and Sataw Beans
blocks.descHtml:
Ko Choi is a long-established Thai-Chinese restaurant in Trang that has stood at the Ko Choi junction near Kra Phang Surin pond for several decades — so long that the restaurant's name has become the name people use for that intersection. If you want flavours from your parents' generation — large sharing plates, family-style — this is the place. It works well for families wanting a proper sit-down meal while in Trang, or groups of friends who want tried-and-tested local dishes without having to guess.

The most talked-about dish is the red-braised pork leg — tender meat, skin that still has a pleasant bounce without turning mushy, and a sauce that is sweet-savoury with a gentle sour note so it doesn't cloy. Another unmissable item is Ko Choi's cold pork leg — a style that is rare to find elsewhere, served with pickled ginger and peanuts to cut through the richness. For rice dishes, the bitter-gourd curry with sea-bass fillet and young coconut shoot is a must: a deep, fragrant broth, not explosively spicy, smooth on the palate, with firm fish. And the shrimp stir-fried with shrimp paste and sataw beans brings an aromatic shrimp-paste hit with punchy flavour — excellent with steamed rice.

Reviews broadly describe it as old-school flavour that recalls childhood meals — generous portions, good value. Price per person is approximately 101–250 THB, reasonable given the portions and skill. Open daily roughly 10:00–20:00. Street parking nearby the intersection, easy by car.

Worth noting: the dining room is an older shophouse, a little dark, and not decorated for aesthetics. Come for the food. The lunch rush on weekends is busy; allow extra time. If there are only a few of you, order judiciously because the dishes tend to be large. For genuine old Trang flavour, this spot deserves a place on your list.
mustOrder: Bitter Gourd Curry with Sea Bass and Young Coconut Shoot
Shrimp Stir-fried with Shrimp Paste and Sataw Beans
blocks.spice: Not explosively spicy (bitter gourd curry / shrimp-paste shrimp can be bold)
blocks.libCredit: Illustration: Khao Kha Moo · User:Bi89 / Wikimedia (CC BY-SA 3.0)

blocks.name: Cake Tha Pap
blocks.signature: Young Coconut Topping Cake, Fresh Pandan Butter Cake, Soft Trang City Cake
blocks.descHtml:
If you ask locals in Trang where to buy cake, Cake Tha Pap comes up first almost every time. The shop sits on the Trang–Phatthalung road, across from Rim Nathi Hotel — a pink shop front that stands out from the roadside. Easy roadside parking. It's ideal for anyone driving through who wants to pick up a fresh-baked souvenir, or for those who prefer daily-made cake with no preservatives.

The headliner is the young coconut topping cake — widely described as one of the must-buys of Trang. The cake is light and airy, with a thin layer of cream topped generously with fresh young coconut strips. Sweetness is well judged — present but not cloying. The second most talked-about item is the fresh pandan butter cake: the pandan aroma is clear and distinct, the crumb moist with butter. The soft Trang city cake is a classic Southern-style block with character. Those who want more texture can also choose the jackfruit cake and palm-fruit cake.

Prices are very friendly — the young coconut topping cake is around 100 THB a box, with items starting in the tens of baht. Excellent value as a souvenir. One thing worth knowing: these are fresh cakes with no preservatives, so unrefrigerated they last only one day. The young coconut topping cake sells out fast, especially on holidays — call ahead to be safe.

What has kept this shop at the top of Trang's souvenir list for years is the consistency and the commitment to only making fresh. If it doesn't sell, it goes. Google reviews give it 4.6 stars. Open daily 07:00–18:00. The interior is freshly renovated in a clean minimal style — pleasant to browse the cake display before buying.

blocks.title: 🛏️ Book a Hotel in Trang City
blocks.text: Staying in the Thap Thieng city centre is the most convenient base for eating — roast pork, dim sum, and ancient coffee shops cluster around Huay Yot and Phloen Phithak roads. Wake up and walk or take a short Grab to breakfast. Choose a hotel near the railway station or the clock tower, and you can eat your morning meal and return for a rest before exploring further. Compare room prices and reviews before deciding.

blocks.name: Kopi Satani
blocks.area: Thap Thieng Sub-district, Mueang Trang District, Trang Province
blocks.signature: Ancient Coffee (Kophi), Stuffed Steamed Buns, Baked Spare-rib Rice, Dim Sum
blocks.descHtml:
Kopi Satani is a long-running ancient coffee shop that has been part of Trang for over 30 years, sitting right next to Trang Railway Station. Turn right out of the station and it's less than two minutes on foot. Perfect for anyone who's just stepped off a train and wants something warm before heading out, or for anyone who wants to experience Trang's kophi culture — the Hainanese Chinese coffee ritual — in an authentic setting. The space is two shophouses thrown open together, old chairs and tables in warm tones, feeling like a neighbourhood coffee gathering where the older generation has been sitting since morning.

The most talked-about order is the ancient coffee (kophi), along with iced coffee and iced tea. Multiple reviews say the tea and coffee here are intensely aromatic and strong. Pair them with dim sum or cakes to snack on, and on the food side there are stuffed steamed buns with firm fillings that are good across almost every flavour, hot steamed dim sum, bak kut teh with mantou buns, and the house-made baked spare-rib rice — a signature dish. Several reviewers also highlight the house Southern curry paste, saying it has real heat and depth — genuine Southern Thai spice.

Prices are approachable — coffee and snacks start in the low tens of baht; a full meal is around low-hundreds per person. The bak kut teh is around 135 THB. Open daily 07:30–approximately 16:00. Parking available, credit cards accepted, free Wi-Fi. The most useful feature for travellers is the location — it's the easiest spot in Trang to find — paired with the old-shop character of the place. One stop for dim sum and coffee, Trang-style, complete.

One small note: baked items like the spare-rib rice take a little time to prepare. On busy weekend mornings there may be a short wait. If you're catching a train, stick to dim sum and steamed buns, which come out faster. Overall it's a breakfast and kophi stop that delivers good value and a sense of place.
blocks.bestFor: Breakfast before boarding the train / ancient-coffee and dim-sum fans
blocks.spice: Southern curry paste has a good kick — adjustable

blocks.name: Khao Tom Sri Bun Ruean
blocks.area: Thap Thieng Sub-district, Mueang Trang District, Trang Province
blocks.signature: Jok Kuay Rice Porridge, varied Chinese-Southern sides cooked fresh and hot
blocks.descHtml:
If you're in Trang and want to eat the way locals actually eat at night, Khao Tom Sri Bun Ruean is one of the first names people mention. This restaurant has been part of Trang city for over 30 years — started by the parents, now in its third generation. The bright red shopfront stands at the Wang Yao Bridge traffic-light intersection on Rasdanuphat Road and is impossible to miss. It serves Teochew Chinese-style rice porridge (jok kuay) blended with Southern Thai sides, where the side dishes are laid out to point at, izakaya-style. Good for groups, families, or night owls who want hot porridge with freshly wok-tossed sides.

The dish everyone orders is yam chat na — the restaurant's signature plate — combining crispy pork, fried beans, Chinese sausage, crispy fish, salted egg, and more, tossed together for a full spectrum of flavours in one bowl. Another essential is the hot-plate aw suan (crispy-pork oyster omelette), crispy pork stir-fried with egg yolk, stir-fried curry-spiced sides, orange-broth sour curry with fish (gaeng som pa eh za pla), and the stir-fried Southern-spiced prawn that reviewers say is fragrant with curry paste. For soup alongside the porridge there is also tom kiam buay minced pork. The kitchen uses traditional Chinese seasonings, Pattalung-Trang black pepper, and house-made condiments throughout.

Reviews broadly agree: well-balanced flavours, not overly salty or spicy, the whole family can eat. Prices are very approachable — sides start from 40 THB per dish, averaging around 101–250 THB per person; fish dishes are by weight, starting around 250 THB to feed four to five people. The restaurant opens in the evening and is open late — daily approximately 16:00–00:30, with Friday to Sunday extending to about 1:00 a.m. — making it the after-work gathering place for Trang people.

What keeps this restaurant popular across generations is not just longevity — it's the fact that every dish is made in-house, quality-controlled, with fresh daily ingredients and signature items you can't find elsewhere. Worth knowing: evenings only; lunch is not served. On holiday weekends it gets crowded. For a large group, allow some extra wait time — but freshly wok-tossed dishes straight from the kitchen are worth it.
mustOrder: Yam Chat Na (signature mixed salad plate)
Crispy Pork Stir-fried with Egg Yolk
blocks.bestFor: Late-evening dinner with family or friends

blocks.name: Phong Ocha
blocks.signature: 200+ types of dim sum, Trang roast pork, various rice toppings, coffee
blocks.descHtml:
If you're looking for the breakfast that genuinely represents Trang, Phong Ocha is the name locals say first. This restaurant has been part of the city for over forty years, passed down through generations until it now has three branches in the district — on Huay Yot Road (branch 1) and Phloen Phithak Road (branch 2). The selling point is dim sum in the hundreds — laid out in bamboo baskets — plus Trang roast pork char-grilled over charcoal until fragrant. Perfect for anyone who wants an authentic Southern Thai breakfast experience, a family or group who want to order widely and share.

The dish at virtually every table is Trang roast pork — three-layer pork, crispy skin, fragrant, marinated Cantonese-style — paired with shumai with large dumplings, har gao, hoy jo, and steamed buns. For soup lovers, the bak kut teh hot pot is essential. For sweets, pa thong ko with custard dip rounds off the meal, followed by kophi ancient coffee or a strong tea — reviewers say it's brewed with real depth. What many reviews agree on is that the dim sum arrives hot with firm, well-textured filling — some say it's good enough to eat without dipping sauce.

Prices are as approachable as a local breakfast should be. Dim sum baskets from around 20 THB, a small plate of roast pork around 70 THB, averaging low hundreds to just over 200 THB per person with multiple orders. The atmosphere is round Chinese tables old-style; the Phloen Phithak branch has both air-conditioned and non-air sections seating over a hundred, with free hot tea service. Worth knowing: the restaurant opens very early and items sell out fast. Branches 1 and 2 start around 5:30–6:00 a.m. and close before noon. If you're a late riser, branch 3 opens later.

Phong Ocha has stayed popular across generations because it is the flavour Trang people grew up with — and the first stop most visitors get taken to. Parking is limited; most people park on the street or at a nearby petrol station and walk in. On weekends the best baskets go fast — come early for the full selection.
mustOrder: Dim Sum (Shumai / Har Gao / Hoy Jo)

blocks.name: Hat Yao Seafood
blocks.area: Hat Yao Pier entrance, Kantang District, Trang Province
blocks.signature: Chilli-sauce Grouper, Sour Curry with Crab Roe, Spicy Stir-fried Mixed Seafood, Blanched Cockles, Blue Crab
blocks.descHtml:
Drive to the southern end of Kantang, almost to the end of the road at Hat Yao Pier, and the restaurant everyone points you to first is Hat Yao Seafood — an open-air, sea-breeze-catching spot that has been open for over 25 years, just before the pier. Fishing boats come and go on the water in front of the restaurant. It's a great choice if you're about to board a boat to Koh Libong or Koh Muk, or if you've spent a day on the Trang coast and want to close with a proper seafood meal and a beautiful view.

Regulars order large whole grouper in chilli sauce — firm flesh and bold flavour — sour curry with crab roe in the full Southern Thai style (sour-leading, assertive), spicy stir-fried mixed seafood fragrant with fingerroot, freshly blanched cockles, and blue crab that many reviewers describe as sweet-fleshed. For something unusual, try freshly shucked horseshoe clam. Seafood is priced by weight: fresh blue crab around 700 THB per piece, steamed sea-bass with lime around 450 THB, stir-fried squid in garlic or black ink around 180 THB per dish. Average spend per person is 250–500 THB — fair for the freshness on offer. Reviews broadly praise the ingredients as genuinely fresh, seasoning that isn't toned down for foreign palates, and fast service.

The defining quality of this restaurant's long run is the location and the authentically local feel. Most customers are locals and those boarding boats — not a tourist-tour restaurant — so the food is seasoned like proper Southern Thai. Late afternoon here, with sea breeze and soft light, the pier view is at its best.

Worth knowing: the restaurant is about 50–60 km from Trang city — allow for driving time. Closed Wednesdays. Open approximately from 10 a.m. to early evening. On weekends it fills up — call ahead to book a table or reserve a fine blue crab.
blocks.bestFor: Pre-boat seafood lunch before Koh Libong or Koh Muk; closing a Trang coast day in the evening
blocks.spice: Bold Southern Thai heat (sour curry / spicy stir-fry)

blocks.name: Cake Khuk Ming Lamphura
blocks.area: Lamphura Sub-district, Huay Yot District, Trang Province
blocks.signature: Original Trang Cake — dense texture similar to kanom khai, hole in the centre, no cream icing
blocks.descHtml:
When people talk about Trang's definitive souvenir, Cake Khuk Ming Lamphura is where it all starts. This shop is the true originator of Trang cake — begun by Khuk Ming Sae-Heng, a Hainanese Chinese who settled in Lamphura about 80 years ago and developed his own cake recipe until it became the province's signature sweet. If you want the authentic original — not a later imitation — and a souvenir that tells the full story of Trang in one box, this is the place.

The dish to order is the original egg-flavour cake: a round shape with a hole in the centre, like a donut in form. The texture is dense and similar to kanom khai. No cream, no icing — nothing on top. What reviewers consistently say is that the crumb is "firm but soft", with a clear egg fragrance and well-judged sweetness. It goes beautifully with coffee or tea in the morning. Beyond the original egg flavour, there are also pandan, coffee, orange, three-flavour, and egg-yolk thread varieties — multiple flavours available in one box. The shop's point of pride: no baking powder and no preservatives. Made fresh daily — must be eaten within a few days.

Prices are very reasonable — starting around 80 THB per piece, rarely above the hundreds. The shop is on the Phetchakasem Highway in Lamphura sub-district, Huay Yot District, about 14 km from Trang city. Open daily 06:00–19:00. There's a rush in the late morning and late afternoon; parking is limited.

This shop remains popular across generations because it is both a delicious product and a piece of local history — made by hand in the same way it always has been. Worth knowing: no preservatives means it doesn't keep long. If buying as a gift for a distant trip, factor in travel time. For the best selection of flavours, come in the morning when the trays are full.
mustOrder: Original Egg Cake (with hole in the centre)
blocks.bestFor: Trang souvenir hunters and those who want the traditional original

blocks.title: Know Before You Eat in Trang

items.title: Getting Around
items.text: In the Thap Thieng city centre, several good restaurants are close together and walkable. Grab is easy here. Hat Yao Seafood in Kantang is around 40 minutes away — you'll need a rental car or a hired vehicle.

items.title: Bring Cash
items.text: Old-school shops, market stalls, and most roast-pork sellers take cash only. Carry small bills. Some larger, newer restaurants accept PromptPay.

items.title: Go Early to Beat the Queue
items.text: Morning roast pork and dim sum sell out fast — especially Moo Yang Ko Phao, which is typically gone before 9 a.m. Arriving before 8 a.m. gives you the freshest items without a long wait.

items.title: Language and Menus
items.text: Most local restaurants have Thai-only menus. Staff may speak limited English. Try pointing at items or showing the translated name on your phone. Trang locals are friendly and always happy to point you to the best dish.

items.title: Tipping
items.text: Tipping is not expected in most Trang restaurants. Street stalls and morning shops don't expect it. Leaving small change or rounding up at a place you enjoyed is a nice gesture — always appreciated.

items.title: Seafood by Weight
items.text: Seafood restaurants like Hat Yao Seafood price crabs, prawns, and lobster by the kilogram. Ask the per-kg price and watch the weighing before cooking so there are no surprises at the bill.

blocks.title: Plan a Full Day of Eating in Trang
blocks.html:
Eating in Trang means starting early. Roast-pork and dim-sum spots like Trang Moo Yang, Ruean Thai Dim Sum, and Phong Ocha open from 5 a.m. and close at noon. Moo Yang Ko Phao at the municipal market sells out even faster — often before 9 a.m. If you're serious about catching it, go first thing or call to reserve. For breakfast, set up a plate of crispy roast pork and a couple of dim-sum baskets, then finish with a cup of kophi at Kopi Satani near the railway station.

Mid-morning, stop by for cakes to take home. Cake Tha Pap in Na Yong Tai is the one for young-coconut topping cake; Cake Khuk Ming — the original — is in Lamphura, Huay Yot, a short drive out of town. For lunch through to evening, head to Ko Choi or Khao Tom Sri Bun Ruean in the city. If you have time to drive, the 40-minute run to Hat Yao Seafood in Kantang gets you fresh seafood at the pier with a proper sea view. This sequence covers both savoury and sweet in a single day.

blocks.text: Spending a few days in Trang is easy when you're well placed. Book a hotel in the Thap Thieng city centre and you can walk to roast pork and dim sum in the morning, come back to rest, then head out again for the evening meal.

faq.q: Which restaurant in Trang is the most famous?
faq.a: For the city's signature breakfast, Trang Moo Yang on Huay Yot Road and Ruean Thai Dim Sum on Phloen Phithak are the two names locals and food enthusiasts mention most. For roast pork to take home, Moo Yang Ko Phao at the municipal market is the one people queue for from early morning.

faq.q: What are the signature dishes of Trang you must try?
faq.a: Crispy-skin Trang roast pork with a sweet-leading flavour, hot steamed dim sum, kophi ancient coffee, and soft Trang city cake. The first three can be found at Trang Moo Yang, Ruean Thai Dim Sum, and Phong Ocha. For the authentic original cake, Cake Khuk Ming in Lamphura is the one.

faq.q: How much does food in Trang cost?
faq.a: A roast-pork and dim-sum breakfast runs roughly 100–250 THB per person. Coffee and snacks at Kopi Satani start at around 60 THB. A box of Trang cake is 60–100 THB. Seafood at Hat Yao Seafood is around 250–500 THB per person because fresh ingredients are priced by weight.

faq.q: Do I need to book in advance?
faq.a: Most morning restaurants are walk-in only, but you should arrive early because items sell out. Moo Yang Ko Phao is best reserved by phone in advance. For Hat Yao Seafood, if you're coming in a large group or on a holiday, calling ahead is wise.

faq.q: Which restaurants are open for dinner or late at night?
faq.a: Most roast-pork and dim-sum shops close at noon. For evening dining, Khao Tom Sri Bun Ruean near Wang Yao Bridge is open until after midnight. Ko Choi is open until early evening. Hat Yao Seafood in Kantang is best for a lunch-to-evening outing with sea air.
